accuracy.evidence: Placement checked against Letters and Sounds (DfES 2007) Phase One Aspect 3 'Voice sounds' (copy-cat voice games, animal noises, sound stories, exploring the sounds the voice can make) and Development Matters (DfE 2021) 3-4 Literacy 'develop their phonological awareness' and Communication and Language 'use a wider range of vocabulary'. The long/short split is the phonetic continuant/stop distinction: s, m, f, z, sh, n can be held for a whole breath; t, p, k, b, d, g are plosives that release at once and can only be repeated (Ladefoged and Johnson, A Course in Phonetics). z is voiced and s voiceless, so a hand on the throat feels a hum for zzz only. Volume and pitch are kept as separate properties of a sound, as in the KS2 sound unit.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips named in the adult text: calling t-t-t-t long because it lasted (prediction 1, 'repeat' when a stop goes in the Long box or a dot is needed in a pattern, m3, p2), refusing to stretch a continuant ('cut'), confusing the voiced buzz with the hiss (snake vs bee, 'hum', p3, m9), matching a long sound to a ticking thing ('short'), and treating loud as low or quiet as high (loud mouse and quiet bear rounds on the ladder with 'mixhigh' and 'quiethigh', prediction 3, p5, m2). The adult text also warns against adding uh to stops (tuh, puh).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagvoxsnd is about the child's own voice, not words or outside noises: a stretch handle whose ribbon keeps growing for sss and mmm but stops dead at a short width for t and p, a voice bubble given to a drawn snake, bee, clock or car, a three-stop volume slider fitted to a sleeping baby, a table and a far-off friend, a vertical high-middle-low ladder that separates pitch from volume, and a long-bar/short-dot pattern builder. 982 Telling sounds apart (flagears) identifies outside sources, 457 Making loud and quiet sounds (flagloud) hits and shakes objects, 492 Pitch of sounds uses instruments; none works with voice length or voicing. Shingle similarity to every other flag_*.js is under 30% (gate passes).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds each idea by doing it: dragging the handle on t stops the ribbon at once and reads 'It stopped at once!', while sss keeps growing; only then are the boxes used, and a wrong box explains why. The voice bubble is refused on the wrong thing with the reason (hum, short or long). The slider says 'too loud' or 'too quiet' for the place with why. On the ladder the loud mouse and quiet bear are refused if placed by volume. The pattern builder refuses a dot for a long sound. Done messages only confirm after the actions.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Yes: t-t-t-t-t' for stretching t (the handle stops at once), 'Yes, they both hiss' for the bee (zzz is refused on the snake and sss on the bee, with the hum reason), and 'Yes, quiet sounds are high' for the quiet bear growl (placing it high is refused: a quiet sound can be low).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions whose wrong answers give distinct slip messages: repeat ('saying it again and again is not stretching it'), volume ('Loud is not long. A loud t still stops at once'), mixhigh ('Loud is not low... still a high squeak'), quiethigh, nopitch, place ('A calling voice does not fit. The baby is asleep'), hum ('Put a hand on your throat'), short ('t is short and quick. A bee makes one long sound') and thing. Checked in the browser that each message names the chosen answer.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs score between -1.7 and 0.5 Flesch-Kincaid grade (family kid limit 5.0) with one-idea sentences (Say sss like a snake. Keep it going.). Lab text is two to seven words per card, made to be read aloud by a grown-up, with drawn pictures on every thing. Adult text averages 6.7 (limit 10) while keeping the precise terms: continuant, stop (plosive), voiced, voiceless, phonological awareness, volume and pitch.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one contrast (long, short, loud/quiet, high/low). Adult paragraphs give curriculum placement, the phonetics behind long and short with the voicing note, the named mistakes with how to say stops, and what each lab scene does. No content-gate filler phrase matches; lab strings are only instructions, the sounds and feedback.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes before and after Show me: the stretch ribbon and handle fit beside the sound card, the Long and Short boxes hold their sorted sounds, the 2 by 2 picture grid shows snake, bee, clock and car with labels, the volume slider labels whisper, talking voice and calling voice without clipping, the ladder labels sit left of the rungs, and the pattern slots and two block buttons fit across. Buttons below the canvas wrap onto two rows with large tap targets.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Stretch it, Long box, Short box; one button per thing; Quieter, Louder, Say it; high, middle, low; Long bar and Short dot. The canvas aria-label is replaced with each scene description and every piece of feedback; the challenge feedback is a role=status live region; right and wrong cards carry check and cross text as well as colour. walk.cjs runs axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13.
